case_name: Rohit Laxmidas Sonkawde And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Maharashtra And Another, Nisha (wife)

facts_of_case: Parties arrived at amicable settlement due to intervention of respectable members. They decided to get separated and filed petition No.F-156/2021 before the Famill Court for divorce on mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
legal_principles.held: The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in understanding the court's power to quash criminal proceedings

legal_principles.principle: The High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime before exercising its power to quash a criminal proceeding or complaint.
legal_principles.held: However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — significance in understanding the court's approach to quashing criminal proceedings

outcome.final_order: Quashing of F.I.R. and proceedings vide R.C.C. No. 104/2019 pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class at Latur.

use_for_drafting: quashing FIR in domestic violence cases
